allowed_paths_create: research/governance/COLLECTOR_READINESS_REPORT_V2.json -- created after the single approved formal G4/G5 re-verification run, regardless of PASS or FAIL; immutable historical evidence once written, same as V1

budget_overrides.note: MAX_G4_G5_REVERIFICATION_RUNS=1 and MAX_LIVE_SOAK_RUNS=1 refer to the SAME single 60-minute run, not two separate runs -- this changeset gets exactly one real live re-verification, consumed once. MAX_NEW_DIRS=0 applies to new repository directories; one bounded OS-temp runtime/evidence directory for that single approved re-verification run is permitted and is not counted as a new repo artifact (same convention as NEXT_DATASET_COLLECTOR_READINESS's soak_test_policy.output_location).

reuse_policy: EvidenceHunter_resource_sampling.py and tests/test_resource_sampling.py are reused from the existing draft. Independent review (Claude, 2026-09-08) found the identity-verification design (worker self-reports OS-derived worker_pid/creation_filetime/image_path over a nonce handshake; the orchestrator independently re-verifies the same values via its own OpenProcess/QueryFullProcessImageNameW/GetProcessTimes calls against that exact PID before trusting it) directly addresses the launcher/child-PID defect, and confirmed the worker's runpy.run_path() invocation of EvidenceHunter_collector.py uses that script's real --runtime-dir/--duration-seconds CLI flags correctly, with zero modification to EvidenceHunter_collector.py itself. Only an approved cosmetic fix is in scope: the module docstring's '--probe' should read '--probe-run' to match the actual implemented CLI flag name; no functional rewrite.

readiness_reevaluation_policy.g8_disposition: G8's implementation (evaluate_startup_gate() in EvidenceHunter_collector_readiness.py) is NOT reopened or modified. Its startup-guard verdict is mechanically recomputed by that same unmodified code against the full new gate_results (G1/G2/G3/G6/G7 carried forward unchanged plus the newly re-evaluated G4/G5). If either G4 or G5 still yields any BLOCKING finding, the startup guard correctly continues to block: V2.readiness=FAIL, V2.formal_dataset_start_allowed=false. If G4 and G5 both PASS, the startup guard's verdict becomes V2.readiness=PASS, V2.formal_dataset_start_allowed=true -- this authorizes ONLY a future, separate Dataset-start changeset to proceed; it does not itself create or start a Dataset, and this changeset does not open one.
readiness_reevaluation_policy.validator_tool: EvidenceHunter_collector_readiness.py is expected to require ZERO code changes for this re-evaluation -- the new harness's process_samples.json/process_exit_evidence.json/soak_summary.json schemas already match what the existing G4/G5 validators read. If a real run reveals an actual schema mismatch, that is reported back to PROJECT_OWNER/GPT before any validator edit is proposed, never silently patched.
readiness_reevaluation_policy.report_output: research/governance/COLLECTOR_READINESS_REPORT_V2.json is generated exactly once, after the single approved re-verification run, regardless of its PASS or FAIL outcome. It is immutable historical evidence once written, on the same footing as V1: never overwritten by any later report. A third attempt, if ever needed, would require a new changeset and a new report file (e.g. _V3).

prohibited_this_round: 168h or any long-running unattended live collection start
